WoW: Forever

Priest

Discipline became a real spec rather than a buff bot — but most of what is written about Priest is BlizzCon demo data that nobody has re-verified.

  1. Home
  2. WoW: Forever
  3. Priest

Read this before using anything below

Two disjoint bodies of Priest information exist, and the detailed one is not the live one. The long talent-by-talent list below comes from the BlizzCon demo build. Its own source says so — the Priest changes are "based largely on the BlizzCon demo build" — and its changelog stops on 15 September, two days before the beta opened. Blizzard's live beta notes contain exactly seven Priest lines across every build to date, all small bug fixes. So the rich material is pre-beta data nobody has re-verified, and the live data is thin. Items marked (demo) mean: Blizzard showed this in September, and nobody has confirmed the numbers survived into the shipping build. The upside of that thinness is itself a finding: Blizzard has not balance-touched Priest once during this beta. No damage, mana or cooldown tuning to any Priest spell has been published. A structural tell worth noticing: in Blizzard's own notes every other class is subdivided by spec. Priest alone is subdivided by race.

The seven live changes

  1. Renew can now land critical hits — framed as a bug fix, which means periodic healing crits by design. A real departure from 1.12.
  2. Power Word: Shield can always overwrite an existing shield on a target without Weakened Soul.
  3. Starshards correctly gains spell-pushback resistance from Twilight Focus.
  4. Dark Sacrifice no longer breaks crowd control that breaks on damage, and its mana gain scales with Spirit.
  5. Gnome's Contingency Plan can now crit.
  6. Gnome's Confounding Flash got a cast visual, retuned Holy rather than Arcane.
  7. Eureka! was nerfed to a flat 10% discount across every class — Priests had 15%.

Talents made baseline

Blizzard named three "tax" talents going baseline game-wide — Divine Spirit, Blessing of Kings and Improved Mark of the Wild — and said "such as", so the list is explicitly partial. Divine Spirit is now a trained spell at level 30, and its duration doubled to an hour. Improved Power Word: Fortitude was removed outright rather than made baseline — worth stating precisely, because "the Fortitude tax is gone" is true while "Fortitude became baseline" is not what any source says. Lightwell was de-talented rather than deleted — still trained at 40. Two further de-taxes are racial rather than talent: Devouring Plague and Fear Ward are now universal to all Priests. Fear Ward paid for it — duration cut from 10 minutes to 3, with a 3-minute cooldown. One stacking conflict this creates: the camping Faction Banner grants Spirit and is exclusive with Divine Spirit, which now matters to every Priest.

Discipline (demo)

The design thrust is stated plainly: rather than raising raw healing, the additions give Discipline "more utility, damage, and damage prevention".

New talentEffect
PenanceChannelled Holy volley that either damages an enemy or heals an ally
Divine AegisCritical heals leave an absorb shield
Renewed HopeDirect heals gain crit against Weakened Soul targets, and cut its duration
Soul WardingPower Word: Shield cooldown −4s, cost −15%
Twin DisciplinesDamage and healing of instant casts
Power in LightSmite and Penance hit harder into Holy Fire
Holy Precision+18% Holy spell hit at 3 ranks

Removed: Unbreakable Will, Improved Power Word: Fortitude, Force of Will, Divine Spirit. Wand Specialization went from 5 ranks to 2 and from 5% to 13% — the only hard numbers in the entire demo talent list. Meditation was massively buffed to 50% at 3 ranks. Power Infusion now requires Penance, coupling Discipline's 31-point to its 21-point for the first time, and it does not grant haste. The intended shape at 60 is a Power Word: Shield uptime engine built on Penance, Soul Warding and Renewed Hope. That is design intent, not a tested rotation.

Holy (demo)

Removed: Improved Prayer of Healing and Lightwell, vanilla's 31-point capstone — which is now Prayer of Mending. New: Prayer of Mending fires when the target takes damage or receives non-periodic healing, then jumps, up to five times. Binding Heal heals target and Priest simultaneously at low threat. And Litany of Light restores mana when you cast a healing spell different from your previous one — an explicit anti-spam mechanic, and the biggest change to how Holy plays. Healing Focus is renamed Twilight Focus and now protects any spell, not just heals. Spirit of Redemption makes every healing spell free and lasts 15 seconds rather than 10. Prayer of Healing was reworked and heavily nerfed — roughly a 38% throughput cut plus a targeting change: it now heals a chosen target's party at 40 yards, rather than your own party at 30.

Shadow (demo)

Shadow Weaving was redesigned and it is the most consequential change in the tree. It no longer debuffs the target's Shadow damage taken — it now increases the Priest's own Shadow damage, stacking to five. That un-couples it from raid stacking, from other Shadow Priests, and from Warlock synergy, which the community resents. Shadowform was rebuilt: +10% Shadow damage, −50% Shadow mana cost, +100% Shadow crit damage bonus, −15% physical damage taken. And the lockout changed from "cannot cast Holy spells" to "cannot cast healing spells" — a real widening, since Smite, Holy Fire and Resurrection become legal in Shadowform. Shadow Word: Death is a new baseline spell with a clause nobody's coverage mentions: "If your target is not killed by Shadow Word: Death, you take backlash damage equal to 10% of your maximum health." Silence now interrupts an active cast as well as locking out; in 1.12 it did not interrupt. There is no snapshotting in Forever. Every vanilla DoT-snapshotting habit is dead.

Rotation at 20

The beta cap is 20, so every Priest rotation in existence is a level-20 rotation — and the wand is a load-bearing rotational button in all three specs. Damage filler, all specs: Fortitude and Inner Fire, Power Word: Shield before the pull, Holy Fire (Discipline), Smite as it closes, Mind Blast, Shadow Word: Pain, then wand it down. At 20 Shadow opens with Smite and has no Mind Flay step. Healing: Power Word: Shield to buy cast time, Heal for throughput, Renew for chip damage or while moving. The stated failure mode is worth quoting: "The main reason you'll die while playing as a Priest is running out of mana while still fighting against a healthy foe." But the wand advice is already stale. The 24 September build shipped "wands no longer gain any additional damage from the user's spell damage", and Blizzard has a further wand nerf queued. Any guide recommending wand-weaving as the mana solution needs that caveat. There is no level-60 rotation from any source, and we will not construct one.

Stats

The five-second rule survives intact, and Forever's version has confirmed detail:

  • It keys on cast completion — cancelling or being interrupted does not start the lockout.
  • MP5 ignores the rule entirely, which is why it sits second for healers rather than third.
  • Bypasses are Meditation and Spirit Tap, and Forever's Spirit Tap can now carry regeneration through casting.
  • Downranking is still live and still advised.

Discipline and Holy: Healing Power first — and the reasoning is mana, not throughput, since casting less often to heal the same amount frees GCDs. Then MP5, Spirit, Intellect, and Critical Strike, which is called "an amazing stat" for Discipline specifically because it drives Renewed Hope and Divine Aegis. Shadow: Spell Power, Crit, Hit, Intellect, Stamina, MP5. Hit is deliberately deprioritised at 20, with the note that it takes centre stage at endgame. Since hit is now one unified stat, that endgame hit requirement is the Priest's biggest open gearing question.

Race

Priest races: Human, Dwarf, Night Elf, Gnome, Undead, Troll. Not Orc, not Tauren, and not Skyborne.

AbilityForever status
Devouring PlagueUniversal to all Priests
Fear WardUniversal, but cut to 3 minutes
Desperate PrayerDwarf keeps it, Human loses it for new Divine Grace
ChastiseNew, Dwarf only — a Humanoid soft-CC that immobilises
Elune's GraceReworked — now covers melee and ranged, dodge 10% → 50%
StarshardsDamage nearly doubled, gained a 30-second cooldown
Touch of Weakness / Hex of WeaknessKept, both rewritten to reduce melee attack power
Symbol of HopeNot present, and a false premise — it is a TBC Draenei ability

New Undead racial, Dark Sacrifice: trades your own health over 15 seconds for mana, scaling with Spirit. With Cannibalize now restoring mana as well as health, Undead gets a real two-minute mana cooldown — which is why every recommendation puts Undead first on Horde. New Human racial, Divine Grace: heals a target below 50% health and removes Weakened Soul from them. That second clause is a Power Word: Shield reset. Gnome Priest is the new combo, and it is contentious. Confounding Flash confuses up to five enemies; Contingency Plan wards an ally and pays out when they drop below 35% health. It is compared to retail's Guardian Spirit, and Icy Veins expects it to be reworked, noting the Gnome racials "are causing an uproar". One careful counter-reading: Contingency Plan is not a death save — it pays out only after the target has already fallen that low. Weapon-skill racials became caster racials. A Human Priest wielding a sword gets +2% spell crit. Picks, all provisional: Gnome overall on Alliance, with Human a genuine toss-up for Discipline; Night Elf for Alliance Shadow, because Elune's Light is a crit burst window made more valuable by the absence of snapshotting; Undead for every Horde spec.

Still unknown

Which talents occupy the 16-point row — derivations disagree, and one client read suggests Shadow may have none. Contingency Plan's max-rank values, which the client does not ship. Almost every Priest spell value: Greater Heal, Flash Heal, Prayer of Healing, Mind Blast, Holy Nova, Dispel, Inner Fire, Shackle Undead, Psychic Scream and Resurrection have no published changes and no published confirmations of non-change. Mass Dispel most likely does not exist, as it was never a 1.12 ability.
